title: Abdul El-Sayed Wins Michigan Race to Become First Muslim Elected to US Senate
excerpt: The 42-year-old former Wayne County health director defeated Republican Mike Rogers in the open-seat race, holding a must-win seat for Democrats as they retook both chambers.
body:
• Democrat Abdul El-Sayed has won Michigan's open US Senate seat, becoming the first Muslim elected to the Senate, according to the Associated Press and media projections.
  • The AP called the race at 2:27 a.m. ET with El-Sayed leading Republican Mike Rogers 52% to 46% — 2,355,790 votes to 2,069,010 with about 86% of precincts reporting.
  • El-Sayed, 42, a physician and epidemiologist born in Michigan to Egyptian immigrant parents, succeeds retiring Democrat Gary Peters.
  • The hold keeps a must-win battleground seat in Democratic hands on a night the party retook both chambers of Congress.

Abdul El-Sayed, a former Wayne County health director who ran as an unapologetic progressive, has won Michigan's open US Senate seat and will become the first Muslim elected to the Senate, according to Reuters and projections by the Associated Press, Fox News and Decision Desk HQ. He defeated former Republican congressman Mike Rogers, preserving a seat Democrats could not afford to lose in their fight for Senate control.

The result

The Associated Press called the race at 2:27 a.m. ET. With about 86% of precincts reporting, El-Sayed led Rogers by roughly 52% to 46% — 2,355,790 votes to 2,069,010. He declared victory to supporters in Detroit at about 1:30 a.m., before the race was formally called. In his victory remarks, reported by ANI, he told supporters that America is "big enough for all of us."

https://x.com/RadioGenoa/status/2117878680630227215

"America is big enough for all of us."

— Abdul El-Sayed, in his victory remarks in Detroit

Who he is

El-Sayed, 42, was born in Michigan to Egyptian immigrant parents. A physician and epidemiologist, he served as Detroit's health director and then as Wayne County's health director before entering the race for the seat vacated by retiring Senator Gary Peters, who is stepping down after two terms. According to Reuters, he campaigned on lowering costs for working families and reducing corporate influence in politics, and his victory marks a breakthrough for the Democratic Party's progressive wing.

A bitter campaign

Rogers, 63, a former congressman and FBI agent backed by President Trump and national Republicans, sought to cast El-Sayed as a radical sympathetic to Islamic extremism through alleged ties to the Muslim Brotherhood — claims El-Sayed denies and that Reuters notes remain unsupported by evidence. The race also split Democrats: two days before the election, Representative Haley Stevens, whom El-Sayed had beaten in the primary, pulled her endorsement and backed Rogers, according to the Wall Street Journal. El-Sayed won anyway, in a state Trump carried by 1.4 points in 2024.

Why it matters beyond Michigan

Republicans held a 53–47 Senate majority going into Tuesday's midterms, and Democrats needed a net gain of four seats to take control; Michigan's seat was widely seen as necessary to that path. For Muslim Americans and the wider immigrant diaspora, the result is a representation milestone: Muslims have served in the House of Representatives, but none had previously been elected to the Senate. El-Sayed will be sworn in when the new Congress takes office in January.
nri_angle: A first-Muslim-in-the-Senate milestone in a midterm where diaspora and immigrant communities were central to the story.
